classification.difficultyReason: Find intersections, identify the upper parabola and integrate the difference.

content.prompt: Solve simultaneously, sketch, shade the enclosed region, and find its area for:

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}x^2-x+4&=-x^2+3x+4\\2x^2-4x&=0\\2x(x-2)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }x=2\end{aligned}$$
Intersections: $(0,4)$ and $(2,6)$.
The second parabola is above the first on $[0,2]$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_0^2\bigl((-x^2+3x+4)-(x^2-x+4)\bigr)\,dx\\&=\int_0^2(4x-2x^2)\,dx\\&=\left[2x^2-\frac{2x^3}{3}\right]_0^2\\&=8-\frac{16}{3}\\&=\frac83\text{ u}^2\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Two unshaded parabolas with arrowheads, labelled axes and no ticks or point labels. Ordinary source blue strokes become black.
spec.mathematics: The curves intersect at (0,4) and (2,6); their vertices are (1/2,15/4) and (3/2,25/4).
